## Additional reproduction scenario: file extension vs actual MIME type mismatch

@thdxr I hit the exact same "poisons subsequent turns" issue, but with a more specific root cause worth noting:

### What happened

1. Used bash tool to call Gemini API for image generation. Gemini returned `mimeType=image/jpeg` data.
2. The AI-written script saved the JPEG data with a `.png` extension: `/tmp/nano_banana_test.png`
3. AI then called the `read` tool on this `.png` file
4. **OpenCode's read tool correctly detected** the attachment mime as `image/jpeg` (stored correctly in the DB with `"mime":"image/jpeg"` and `"url":"data:image/jpeg;base64,..."`)
5. **However, when assembling the API request for the next turn**, OpenCode used `media_type: image/png` (inferred from the `.png` file extension), overriding the correctly detected mime
6. Anthropic API returned 400: `"The image was specified using the image/png media type, but the image appears to be a image/jpeg image"`
7. Session permanently stuck - every subsequent turn re-sends the poisoned tool_result

### Key insight

The bug is in the **provider adapter layer**: when converting stored attachments into API request payloads, OpenCode re-infers the media type from the file path extension instead of using the already-correct `mime` field from the stored attachment data.

### Environment

- OpenCode v1.2.27
- macOS (arm64)  
- Anthropic claude-opus-4-6
- Workaround: manually cleaned the SQLite DB (`opencode.db`) - removed the image attachment from the part data and deleted the error messages

I checked the Nix side locally and this looks unrelated to the changes in this PR.

This PR only touches:
- `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts`
- `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`
- `packages/opencode/src/tool/bash.ts`
- two test files

It does not touch `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, `nix/*`, or any workflow.

The CI failure is `invalid SRI hash 'TnrYykX8Mf/Ugtkix6V'`, which matches the prefix of the existing `nixpkgs` narHash already in `flake.lock` (`sha256-TnrYykX8Mf/Ugtkix6V+PjW7miU2yClA6uqWl/v6KWM=`). `nix flake metadata` still shows the full hash correctly.

Also, `nix/opencode.nix:28` seems to just be where evaluation forces `${finalAttrs.node_modules}` while computing the derivation. That file is not doing any hash parsing or rewriting.

So this seems more like a pre-existing Nix/CI hash truncation issue in the evaluation path, rather than something caused by this PR.

Having a very quick look around the code base it seems like the `read` tool can also list directory entries but it's no wonder to me that this doesn't work well because
- although "reading a directory" == "listing files" is valid imho this terminology is not often used and hence I would assume models don't necessarily know about it
- the tool spec/description is confusing because it has to mix two functionalities (listing directories and reading file content) of which it focuses on the reading file content functionality and does not say much about listing directories

From https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.3.0/packages/opencode/src/tool/read.txt:
```
Read a file or directory from the local filesystem. If the path does not exist, an error is returned.

Usage:
- The filePath parameter should be an absolute path.
- By default, this tool returns up to 2000 lines from the start of the file.
- The offset parameter is the line number to start from (1-indexed).
- To read later sections, call this tool again with a larger offset.
- Use the grep tool to find specific content in large files or files with long lines.
- If you are unsure of the correct file path, use the glob tool to look up filenames by glob pattern.
- Contents are returned with each line prefixed by its line number as `<line>: <content>`. For example, if a file has contents "foo\n", you will receive "1: foo\n". For directories, entries are returned one per line (without line numbers) with a trailing `/` for subdirectories.
- Any line longer than 2000 characters is truncated.
- Call this tool in parallel when you know there are multiple files you want to read.
- Avoid tiny repeated slices (30 line chunks). If you need more context, read a larger window.
- This tool can read image files and PDFs and return them as file attachments.
```
-> the usage talks about reading file content only

and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.3.0/packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts#L21-L27:
```
  parameters: z.object({
    filePath: z.string().describe("The absolute path to the file or directory to read"),
    offset: z.coerce.number().describe("The line number to start reading from (1-indexed)").optional(),
    limit: z.coerce.number().describe("The maximum number of lines to read (defaults to 2000)").optional(),
  }),
```
-> the params `offset` and `limit` also rather sound like about reading file content

**Update for OpenCode 1.3+ — [opencode-claude-bridge](https://github.com/dotCipher/opencode-claude-bridge) v1.6.1**

For those still hitting issues (especially after the OpenCode 1.3 update that removed the built-in Anthropic plugin), I've released v1.6.1 of `opencode-claude-bridge` with several fixes:

**What was breaking on OpenCode 1.3:**
- The removal of the built-in Anthropic provider meant that OAuth requests were no longer automatically injecting a required `x-anthropic-billing-header` system block — Anthropic's API silently rejects these requests without it
- Some users saw _"Anthropic API key is missing"_ because the SDK required a non-empty key at initialization time even during OAuth flows
- Model selection could break if the plugin's auth loader threw during provider initialization

**What v1.6.1 fixes:**
- Injects the `x-anthropic-billing-header` system block automatically (required for OAuth on OpenCode 1.3)
- Sets a placeholder `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` instead of deleting it, so the SDK initializes cleanly — the real `Authorization: Bearer` token is set in the request headers by the fetch wrapper
- Guards `provider.models` access in case OpenCode 1.3 passes an incomplete provider object during model selection

**Install / upgrade:**
```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-claude-bridge"] }
```
Or upgrade manually:
```bash
cd ~/.cache/opencode && npm install opencode-claude-bridge@latest
```
Then restart OpenCode. If you're logged into Claude CLI (`claude login`), it auto-syncs your credentials — no re-auth needed.

I dug a bit deeper and this looks like a narrow `ProviderTransform.variants()` bug rather than a general Spark outage.

## Root cause

For `@ai-sdk/openai`, `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` currently gives GPT-5 variants:

- `low` / `medium` -> `reasoningSummary: "auto"`
- `high` / `xhigh` -> `reasoningSummary: "detailed"`

That works for most GPT-5 models, but `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` appears to reject the `detailed` summary path while still accepting `auto`.

I verified locally:

- `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` + `low` ✅
- `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` + `medium` ✅
- `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` + `high` ❌ `Unsupported parameter: reasoning.summary`
- `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` + `xhigh` ❌ same error

And forcing Spark `high` / `xhigh` to use `reasoningSummary: "auto"` made both variants work.

## Suggested patch

File:
- `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts`

Minimal fix in the `@ai-sdk/openai` branch of `ProviderTransform.variants()`:

```ts
const isSparkSummaryLimited = id === "gpt-5.3-codex-spark"

return Object.fromEntries(
  openaiEfforts.map((effort) => [
    effort,
    {
      reasoningEffort: effort,
      reasoningSummary:
        isSparkSummaryLimited
          ? "auto"
          : effort === "high" || effort === "xhigh"
            ? "detailed"
            : "auto",
      include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"],
    },
  ]),
)
```

This preserves `reasoningEffort` for Spark while avoiding the known-bad summary shape.

## Regression test

There’s already a good home for this:
- `packages/opencode/test/provider/transform.test.ts`

Suggested test cases:

```ts
test("gpt-5.3-codex-spark uses auto reasoningSummary for high and xhigh", () => {
  const model = createMockModel({
    id: "openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark",
    providerID: "openai",
    api: {
      id: "gpt-5.3-codex-spark",
      url: "https://api.openai.com",
      npm: "@ai-sdk/openai",
    },
    release_date: "2026-01-01",
  })

  const result = ProviderTransform.variants(model)

  expect(result.high).toMatchObject({
    reasoningEffort: "high",
    reasoningSummary: "auto",
  })

  expect(result.xhigh).toMatchObject({
    reasoningEffort: "xhigh",
    reasoningSummary: "auto",
  })
})

test("gpt-5.3-codex keeps detailed reasoningSummary for high and xhigh", () => {
  const model = createMockModel({
    id: "openai/gpt-5.3-codex",
    providerID: "openai",
    api: {
      id: "gpt-5.3-codex",
      url: "https://api.openai.com",
      npm: "@ai-sdk/openai",
    },
    release_date: "2026-01-01",
  })

  const result = ProviderTransform.variants(model)

  expect(result.high?.reasoningSummary).toBe("detailed")
  expect(result.xhigh?.reasoningSummary).toBe("detailed")
})
```

## Why this seems preferable

- very small blast radius
- no retry logic needed
- no global GPT-5 behavior change
- matches observed Spark compatibility exactly

The root cause and expected fix described there appear to be the same issue you're experiencing.

This is related, but I’m not seeing an infinite loop. What happens here is a **single, unwanted continuation** after compaction.

In my case, compaction often runs right before / during / after the agent answers a simple question. I only want the answer - not for the agent to resume previously open tasks.

> [Stops after compaction #13217](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13217): Related — agent stops mid-task after compaction (the inverse behavior, but same underlying compaction/state-tracking problem).

That issue describes the agent stopping mid-task. Here it’s usually the opposite: after compaction, the agent notices remaining tasks and **continues working**, even though no further action was requested.

The common theme seems to be that after `/compact`, the implicit “wait for user input” state isn’t reliably preserved.

Some thoughts I have about this issue:

- After `/compact`, the agent seems to lose the distinction between “actively working on a task” and “waiting for user input”.
- In cases where compaction happens right after answering a question, the agent often resumes remaining work automatically, even though no further action was requested.
- This suggests that compaction is currently context-driven, but not aware of the agent’s current task or wait state.
- From a user perspective, it would be important for `/compact` to preserve whether the agent was in the middle of a task or had naturally reached a point where it should wait.
